title: Mitral inflow arrow at passive ventricular filling = third heart sound (S3)
vignette: The following vignette applies to the next 2 items. A 52-year-old man comes to the office with a 2-week history of shortness of breath and dry cough. The patient has noticed decreased exercise tolerance that limits his daily activities. A Doppler probe placed at the cardiac apex reveals the mitral inflow pattern across the mitral valve: an early, rapid passive-filling wave (E wave), then a period of minimal flow (diastasis), then a later wave from atrial contraction (A wave); an arrow marks the peak of the early passive-filling wave. Item 1 of 2: The point marked by the arrow would best correspond to which of the following auscultation findings?

clues.text: decreased exercise tolerance that limits his daily activities
clues.note: Progressive dyspnea and reduced exercise tolerance suggest heart failure / elevated filling pressures - the setting in which an S3 is heard.

clues.text: an arrow marks the peak of the early passive-filling wave
clues.note: The early, rapid PASSIVE ventricular filling phase (E wave) is when a THIRD heart sound (S3) occurs - from sudden limitation of ventricular movement as blood rushes in.

whatMatters: The arrow marks EARLY, RAPID PASSIVE ventricular FILLING (the E wave). A THIRD HEART SOUND (S3) occurs at this moment - produced by sudden deceleration/limitation of ventricular filling. Answer D.
strategy: Map the mitral inflow waves to heart sounds. Early passive filling (E wave) -> S3 (best heard at the apex, left lateral decubitus; abnormal in patients >40 with dilated/volume-overloaded ventricles). Atrial contraction (A wave, end-diastole) -> S4. Reject S4 (occurs with the A wave, not the E wave), midsystolic click (systole; mitral valve prolapse), and S2 (semilunar valve closure at end of systole - not during diastolic filling).

eliminations.label: Fourth heart sound - occurs with the A wave (atrial contraction)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: S4, a late-diastolic sound coinciding with ATRIAL contraction (the A wave). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the arrow is on the EARLY passive-filling (E) wave, not the atrial (A) wave; S4 would align with the A wave. ✅ Correct if: the point marked were the atrial-contraction (A) wave (S4, stiff ventricle).

eliminations.label: Midsystolic click - systole (mitral valve prolapse)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a click in mid-SYSTOLE (mitral valve prolapse). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it occurs during systole (flow away from an apical probe), not during the diastolic passive-filling wave marked here. ✅ Correct if: mid-systolic click of MVP.

eliminations.label: Second heart sound - semilunar valve closure (end systole)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: S2 from AORTIC/PULMONIC valve closure at the end of systole. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: S2 marks the start of diastole (before filling), not the peak of early passive ventricular filling. ✅ Correct if: end-systolic semilunar valve closure.

reasoning: The arrow marks the early, rapid passive ventricular filling phase (E wave)
A third heart sound (S3) is generated during this passive filling
S3 results from sudden limitation of ventricular movement as blood rushes in
mechanism: Doppler across the MITRAL VALVE shows diastolic left-atrium-to-left-ventricle flow with two peaks: an early, rapid PASSIVE FILLING wave (E WAVE) just after the mitral valve opens, a mid-diastolic pause of minimal flow (DIASTASIS, from pressure equalization), and a late wave produced by ATRIAL CONTRACTION (A WAVE) at end-diastole. Heart sounds map to these phases: a THIRD heart sound (S3) occurs during EARLY passive filling (the E wave), caused by sudden deceleration/limitation of ventricular movement as blood rapidly fills the ventricle - best heard with the bell at the cardiac APEX in the left lateral decubitus position. An S3 can be normal in young adults/high-output states but in patients >40 suggests abnormal ventricular cavity enlargement (chronic severe mitral or aortic regurgitation, dilated cardiomyopathy, heart failure with volume overload). A FOURTH heart sound (S4) instead coincides with the A WAVE (atrial contraction against a stiff ventricle). The S2 marks semilunar valve closure at end-systole, and a midsystolic click occurs in systole - neither aligns with the passive-filling wave. Thus the arrow corresponds to S3.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid CV > heart sounds/cardiac cycle: S3 during early passive ventricular filling (E wave), sudden filling limitation; abnormal >40 (volume overload/dilated ventricle, MR/AR/HF); S4 during atrial contraction (A wave, stiff ventricle); best heard apex/left lateral decubitus.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Arrow at early passive filling (E wave) = S3; atrial contraction (A wave) = S4.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on E wave/A wave, diastasis, S3 vs S4, passive vs active ventricular filling, or mitral inflow Doppler? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: S4 = A wave (atrial contraction); midsystolic click = systole (MVP); S2 = semilunar closure (end systole).

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: Mitral inflow Doppler (stem): arrow on the early rapid passive-filling (E) wave = timing of the third heart sound (S3).

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: S3 = early passive ventricular filling (E wave); S4 = atrial contraction (A wave).

firstAid.detail: CV: early passive filling (E wave); volume overload if >40.
CV > S3 at apex, left lateral decubitus.

memoryHook: Blood rushing in during early filling (E wave) thuds to a stop = S3 (the 'ken-tuc-KY' gallop); the late atrial kick (A wave) is S4.
